title: DerivedValue
description: The carve-out for values that are computed rather than quoted (PLAN.md, 'Python-derived values have no span'). ARR/NNT/effect sizes from clinical_math.py, and GRADE modifiers such as an imprecision downgrade read off a confidence interval, exist in no paper as text — a literal-substring rule would reject them. PLAN.md's sentence is 'the check recomputes the arithmetic', so `operation` is a CLOSED ENUM and not the free-text `formula` the plan sketched: a free-text formula can only be validated for shape, which would leave the recomputation promise unearned. schemas.recompute_derived() evaluates the operation over the operands and rejects a stated result that does not match.

operation.description: difference = minuend - subtrahend (ARR). ratio = numerator / denominator (RRR). reciprocal_abs = 1 / |value| (NNT). ci_includes_null / ci_excludes_null = whether null_value lies inside [ci_low, ci_high] (the GRADE imprecision judgement).

operands.description: Named numeric inputs. The set of names is fixed per operation and enforced in Python; every operand that comes from the paper must be named by one of the input locators.

result.description: The stated result. Recomputed and compared — a number for the arithmetic operations, a boolean for the confidence-interval ones.

inputs.description: Locators for every quoted operand. Their `fields` name operands, not fields of the enclosing record.
